newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-GA life profits lifts H1 to record.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-GA life profits lifts H1 to record.

text.p: Britain's General Accident reported record first half profits on Tuesday as a sharp rise in life profits helped offset difficult general insurance markets worldwide.
But the Scottish-based composite insurer dampened speculation about life acquisitions, at least in the near term.
The group's intention was to concentrate on getting the full benefits from last year's Provident Mutual acquisition before looking at other possible targets, chief executive Bob Scott said.
Over the first six months of 1997, operating profits rose to 260 million pounds, up from 193 million pounds last year.
The figures were at the top end of market forecasts and the shares added 1/2 pence to 945-1/2 pence.
As expected there was little upbeat news on rates and the profit outlook going forward remained tough, analysts said.
Life profits rose 37 percent to 63 million pounds, reflecting the absence of integration costs associated with the Provident Mutual acquisition and the benefits of focusing on growing the business.
Sales of life and pensions products rose 19 percent with a similar increase in the profitability of new business.
GA expects life profits to continue to enjoy the healthy growth seen in the first half over the remainder of 1997.
It has set itself the target of doubling business from sales of life assurance, pension and investment products over the next three years.

In May, it said it hoped to buy two companies, one dealing in life and the other a general insurance concern with small business expertise. But it stressed then that it would not be rushed into purchases.
The general insurance market remained highly competitive in all GA's major territories in the first half.
Net written premiums fell to 2,210 million pounds from 2,230 million pounds while the worldwide underwriting deficit declined to 66 million pounds from 105 million pounds.
The underwriting improvement was helped by a 40 million pound fall in severe weather-related losses to 50 million pounds.
GA again reaped the rewards of its UK branch network and focus on short-tailed personal and small commercial risks, increasing underwriting profits to 19 million pounds.
It is the only major insurer to manage an underwriting profit in the competitive UK market in the first half.
However, rate increases were proving increasingly hard, said Scott.
Overseas markets were similarly competitive with the U.S. unable to break out of its long down cycle and Canada difficult.
There were signs of rate increases being applied by a number of companies in UK private motor, but not in other product lines.
Increases in personal and commercial premiums by GA have stuck but the company has lost some business in commercial as a result of the rise.
Like rivals, GA had seen a sharp increase in UK property subsidence costs to 12 million pounds, an increase of 50 percent from last year.
A similar increase is expected over the full year.
In the U.S., rate increases have proved difficult.
However, the U.S. produced an improved underwriting result, reflecting reduced severe weather costs.
The company has begun a programme of staff reduction, shedding 400 jobs in the first half.
Around 600 jobs are expected to go by the end of the year.
Underwriting losses in Europe increased to 20 million pounds due largely to several large fire losses.
Investment earnings in the half year grew seven percent in original currencies, partly reflecting the move from equities into higher yielding bonds.
GA has reduced equity holdings to around 25 percent, down from 40 percent some 18 months ago.
Total pre-tax profits, including realised investment gains of 334 million pounds rose to 580 million pounds from 335 million pounds.
Net asset value per share rose to 784 pence by August 8 from 675 pence at the end of 1996.
The interim dividend was raised 10 percent to 12.5 pence per share.
